questionText: Listen to a visitor purchasing an annual membership at a city museum front desk.
audioScript:
Situation: A man visits the City Heritage Museum to buy an annual membership and asks about the associated benefits.
Assistant: Good morning, City Heritage Museum, welcome. How can I help you today?
Visitor: Hello, I'd like to buy an annual membership. I came last week and really enjoyed the exhibits.
Assistant: That's lovely to hear. An annual membership is forty-eight pounds for an adult, and it gives you unlimited entry to all permanent and temporary exhibitions.
Visitor: That sounds reasonable. Does it include the special photography exhibition next month?
Assistant: Yes, members get free entry to all temporary exhibitions, plus a ten percent discount in the museum shop and café. You'll also receive our quarterly newsletter by email.
Visitor: Excellent. I'd also like to bring my nephew occasionally. Is that covered?
Assistant: Family membership is eighty-two pounds and covers two adults and up to three children under sixteen. A single adult guest pass costs six pounds per visit on top of your individual membership.
Visitor: I'll go with the individual adult membership for now. Can I pay by card?
Assistant: Of course. We accept Visa and Mastercard but not cash, I'm afraid. The system is card-only since last month.
Visitor: No problem. Here's my card.
Assistant: Thank you. Could you fill in this short form with your name, address, and email? Your membership card will be ready in about five minutes, and it's valid from today for a full twelve months.

questionText: Listen to a parent booking swimming lessons for her child at a leisure centre.
audioScript:
Situation: A woman phones a leisure centre to book beginner swimming lessons for her seven-year-old son.
Receptionist: Good afternoon, Oakfield Leisure Centre, this is Priya speaking. How can I help?
Caller: Hi, I'd like to book swimming lessons for my son. He's seven and a complete beginner.
Receptionist: Certainly. We run group lessons on weekday evenings and Saturday mornings. The beginner stage is called Stage One, and each lesson is thirty minutes long.
Caller: Saturday morning would be best for us. What time?
Receptionist: The Saturday Stage One class runs from nine fifteen to nine forty-five. There's also one at ten thirty, but that's currently full.
Caller: Nine fifteen works. How many children are in a group?
Receptionist: We cap each group at eight children with one qualified instructor and a poolside assistant. The course runs for ten weeks.
Caller: Good. How much does the ten-week course cost?
Receptionist: It's sixty-five pounds for the full course, payable upfront, or you can spread it at seven pounds per week, which works out a little more. We also offer a sibling discount of ten percent if you book for more than one child.
Caller: Just the one for now. Does he need any special equipment?
Receptionist: Just swimwear and a towel. We provide arm bands and floats. All children must wear a swimming cap, which you can buy here for three pounds if you don't have one.
Caller: Great. Can I book the nine fifteen Saturday slot now?
Receptionist: Absolutely. The first lesson starts this coming Saturday the seventh. Please arrive fifteen minutes early to complete a registration form and safety briefing.

questionText: Listen to a patient calling an optician to book an eye test appointment.
audioScript:
Situation: A man phones an optician's practice to book a routine eye test and ask about the cost and what to bring.
Receptionist: Good morning, ClearVision Opticians, this is Hannah. How can I help?
Caller: Hello, I'd like to book an eye test, please. I think my prescription might have changed.
Receptionist: Of course. When did you last have your eyes tested?
Caller: About two years ago, at a different practice. I've moved to this area recently.
Receptionist: No problem. A standard eye test takes around twenty-five minutes and costs thirty pounds. However, if you're over sixty or on certain benefits, it may be free. Are either of those applicable?
Caller: No, I'm forty-three and not on benefits, so I'll pay.
Receptionist: Fine. We have availability on Wednesday at two fifteen, or Thursday at four forty-five. Which would you prefer?
Caller: Thursday at four forty-five, please. It's after work.
Receptionist: Booked. Could I have your full name and a contact number?
Caller: It's Marcus Lindqvist, and my number is oh-seven-eight-nine-two, four-four-one, six-three-zero.
Receptionist: Thank you, Mr. Lindqvist. Please bring your current glasses if you have them, and any previous prescription details. If you wear contact lenses, remove them at least two hours before the test for an accurate result.
Caller: I do wear contacts. I'll make sure to take them out beforehand.
Receptionist: Also, if you'd like to be seen by a specific optometrist, Dr. Lewis is available on Thursdays. Otherwise it will be Dr. Carter.
Caller: Dr. Lewis is fine, thank you.
Receptionist: Excellent. We'll send a text reminder the day before. See you Thursday at four forty-five.

questionText: Listen to a homeowner calling a pest control company about a mouse problem.
audioScript:
Situation: A woman phones a pest control company to report mice in her kitchen and book a treatment visit.
Agent: Good morning, SafeGuard Pest Control, this is Tom speaking. How can I help?
Caller: Hi, I've been hearing scratching in the walls and I found droppings in my kitchen cupboard this morning. I think I have mice.
Agent: I'm sorry to hear that. I can help. First, a few questions. How long have you noticed the signs?
Caller: About three or four days, but the droppings only appeared this morning.
Agent: Understood. We offer a standard residential treatment for mice. The initial visit is seventy-five pounds, which includes a full inspection, placement of bait stations, and advice on proofing. A follow-up visit after two weeks is included in that price.
Caller: That's reasonable. When is the earliest you can come?
Agent: We have a slot tomorrow afternoon between two and four, or Thursday morning between nine and eleven.
Caller: Tomorrow afternoon, please. I work from home so I'm flexible within that window.
Agent: Booked. Could I have your address?
Caller: It's twenty-three Beechwood Avenue, postcode M14 sevenKL.
Agent: Thank you. The technician assigned is called Ravi. He'll need access to the kitchen, loft, and any outbuildings. If you have pets, please keep them out of treated areas for at least twenty-four hours.
Caller: I have a cat. I'll keep her upstairs during the visit and afterwards.
Agent: Perfect. One last thing: if the infestation isn't resolved after the follow-up, a third visit is charged at a reduced rate of forty pounds. Most cases, however, are resolved within two visits.
Caller: Good to know. I'll see Ravi tomorrow between two and four.

questionText: Listen to a customer collecting dry cleaning and asking about a stain removal service.
audioScript:
Situation: A man visits a dry cleaner to collect some items and asks about an additional stain removal service for a jacket.
Assistant: Good afternoon, FreshPress Dry Cleaners, how can I help?
Customer: Hi, I'm here to collect a dry cleaning order under the name Whitfield. It should be ready today.
Assistant: Let me check. Yes, two shirts and one suit, ready for collection. That'll be twenty-four pounds altogether.
Customer: Great. I also have a wool jacket with a red wine stain on the sleeve. Can you treat that?
Assistant: We can certainly try. Red wine on wool is tricky, but our specialist stain removal process has a good success rate. The charge is eight pounds per item, and we'd need it for three working days.
Customer: That's fine. The jacket is quite expensive, so I want it done properly. Is there a guarantee?
Assistant: We can't guarantee complete removal because the stain has set, but if we can't improve it at all, you won't be charged for the stain treatment. You'd still pay the standard dry cleaning fee of twelve pounds for the jacket.
Customer: That seems fair. So the jacket would be twelve plus eight, twenty pounds total?
Assistant: That's right. I'll tag it now. Could you fill in your name and phone number on this slip? We'll text you when it's ready for collection.
Customer: Sure. What are your opening hours? I sometimes work late.
Assistant: We're open Monday to Friday from eight a.m. to seven p.m., and Saturdays from nine to two. We're closed on Sundays and public holidays.
Customer: Perfect, I can pop in after work on a weekday.
Assistant: Your suit and shirts are here in this garment bag. Here's your receipt. The jacket will be ready by Friday.
Customer: Excellent, thank you.

questionText: Listen to a customer calling a courier depot to inquire about a delayed parcel delivery.
audioScript:
Situation: A man phones a courier company's depot to chase a parcel that has not arrived and is now overdue by several days.
Agent: Thank you for calling SwiftParcel customer services, this is James. How can I help?
Caller: Hello, I'm calling about a parcel that was dispatched last Monday and still hasn't arrived. The tracking says it's been at your local depot since Wednesday.
Agent: I'm sorry about the delay. Could I have your tracking number, please?
Caller: Yes, it's S-P-four-seven-Q-R-nine-two-M.
Agent: Thank you. Let me pull that up. I can see the parcel arrived at our Northgate depot on Wednesday at three forty p.m. but wasn't scanned out for delivery. That appears to be an internal processing error.
Caller: That's frustrating. It's a birthday gift for my mother and her birthday is this Saturday, so I really need it by then.
Agent: I completely understand. I've flagged it for priority delivery tomorrow. It will be out on the van by eight a.m. and should reach you between nine and one.
Caller: Thank you. The parcel contains a glass vase. Is it insured?
Agent: Yes, standard cover includes up to fifty pounds. If the contents are worth more, additional compensation can be claimed, but I can see the sender declared a value of seventy-five pounds and purchased extra cover, so you're fully protected up to that amount.
Caller: Good. What happens if it arrives damaged?
Agent: You must report any damage within forty-eight hours of delivery, with photographs of both the item and the packaging. We'll then process a claim within ten working days.
Caller: Understood. Can I change the delivery address to my workplace? I won't be home tomorrow morning.
Agent: I can redirect it to an alternative address, but there's a four pound fifty surcharge for redirection, and it would delay delivery by one more day. Alternatively, you can collect it from the depot today between five and seven p.m. at no extra cost.
Caller: I'll collect it from the depot today. Where exactly are you located?
Agent: We're at Unit twelve, Orbital Industrial Park, Navigator Way. Bring photo ID and the tracking number.
Caller: I'll be there before seven. Thank you for your help.

questionText: Listen to a commuter buying a monthly bus pass at a transport ticket office.
audioScript:
Situation: A woman visits a bus station ticket office to buy a monthly bus pass and asks about zones and top-up options.
Clerk: Good morning, CityBus Travel Centre. How can I help?
Customer: Hi, I'd like to buy a monthly bus pass. I've just started a new job and I'll be commuting every day.
Clerk: Congratulations on the new job. We offer monthly passes for three zones. Zone One covers the city centre, Zone Two adds the inner suburbs, and Zone Three covers the whole network including outer villages.
Customer: I'll be travelling from Greenfield to the city centre. Which zone do I need?
Clerk: Greenfield is in Zone Two, so a Zone One-to-Two pass is what you need. That's fifty-eight pounds per month.
Customer: Does the pass work on all buses or just certain routes?
Clerk: It's valid on all CityBus services within your selected zones, including night buses, but not on express coach services.
Customer: That's fine. Can I load it onto a smartcard?
Clerk: Yes. A smartcard costs three pounds as a one-off fee, and then we load the pass onto it. If you already have one, I can just top it up.
Customer: I don't have one yet, so I'll take a new card. Can I set up automatic monthly renewal?
Clerk: Absolutely. We can set up a direct debit so the pass renews automatically on the first of each month. You'll never have to queue again. Alternatively, you can top up online or at any ticket machine.
Customer: I'll set up the direct debit. What happens if I lose the card?
Clerk: Just call us and we'll block the old card and transfer the pass to a replacement. The first replacement is free, but subsequent ones cost three pounds each. You'll need to verify your identity with your name and address.
Customer: Great. I'll take the smartcard with the Zone One-to-Two pass and set up the direct debit, please.
Clerk: Could you fill in this form? I'll have your card ready in a few minutes.

questionText: Listen to a homeowner calling a gardening service to book a one-off garden clearance.
audioScript:
Situation: A man phones a local gardening company to arrange a one-off garden clearance and lawn treatment after moving into a property with an overgrown garden.
Agent: Good morning, GreenThumb Garden Services, this is Olivia. How can I help?
Caller: Hello, I've just moved into a house and the garden is quite overgrown. I'd like to book a one-off clearance and possibly a lawn treatment.
Agent: Of course. Could you tell me roughly how large the garden is?
Caller: It's a medium-sized back garden, maybe about forty square metres, and there's a small front lawn as well, around ten square metres.
Agent: That's helpful. For a one-off clearance, we charge based on size and condition. A medium garden in poor condition would be around one hundred and twenty pounds. That includes cutting back overgrown shrubs, weeding, removing green waste, and tidying borders.
Caller: That sounds reasonable. What about the lawn?
Agent: We offer a lawn treatment package consisting of scarification, aeration, and fertiliser application. For a combined area of about fifty square metres, that's an additional forty-five pounds. We also reseed bare patches at no extra cost as part of the package.
Caller: I'll take both. How soon can you come?
Agent: Our next available slot is next Tuesday, the eleventh. We'd arrive between eight and ten in the morning and the work typically takes about four hours with a team of two.
Caller: Tuesday works. Do I need to be at home?
Agent: Not necessarily, as long as we have access to the garden. If you have a side gate, please leave it unlocked. We also need access to an outside tap for cleaning tools, if possible.
Caller: The side gate has a padlock. I'll leave it unlocked for you. Do you take the green waste away?
Agent: Yes, all green waste is taken to a licensed recycling facility and the disposal is included in the clearance price. However, any non-green waste, like old bricks or broken furniture, is charged separately at fifteen pounds per load.
Caller: There is an old rusty chair in the back. Would that count?
Agent: Yes, that would be classed as non-green waste, so there'd be a fifteen pound charge for one load. Shall I add that?
Caller: Yes, please. So the total would be one hundred and twenty plus forty-five plus fifteen.
Agent: That's correct, one hundred and eighty pounds in total. We take payment on the day by card or bank transfer. I'll email a confirmation with the date and a checklist of what to prepare.
